retention.stated: Deleted files can be recovered from up to 30 days back.

egress.terms: 'Upload files of any size with unrestricted transfer speeds' — no egress meter quoted on pricing page. Traffic quotas exist on some tiers but not metered per-GB billing.

tooling: rclone backend `pcloud` (long-standing, first-class). WebDAV also offered.
chaining: $250/TB one-time at 2 TB, $150/TB at 10 TB. No account multiplication needed. Family plan 5 users on one quota is the only multiplier.

limits.value: lifetime plans of 500 GB, 2 TB and 10 TB; the largest is 10 TB

limits_note: Storage cap only; 30-day file recovery; encryption (zero-knowledge Crypto folder) is a paid add-on.

identity_cost.detail: a pCloud account is required to buy; payment details are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Longest-running lifetime seller (since 2013), 14-day refund — short window, upload real data inside week one. Best-in-class survival odds among lifetime vendors.
confidence_note: documented: the pages read on 2026-11-03 are three. https://www.pcloud.com/lifetime.html lists the 500 GB, 2 TB and 10 TB lifetime plans at 219 USD, 499 USD and 1499 USD (against 279 USD and 709 USD), as a limited-time promotion that ends on 4/1/2031, once per participant, with no plan transfer between accounts, no combination with other promotions, a pCloud account required to take part, and the money-back guarantee only within the first 14 days after purchase. https://www.pcloud.com/cloud-storage-pricing-plans.html carries the lifetime plans and, in a general file-management list rather than per plan, the lines on upload size, transfer speed and data recovery. https://www.dealkeep.io/blog/pcloud-lifetime-deal repeats the 219, 499 and 1499 USD prices as a third party. The prices, plan sizes and refund window that decide the paid-only verdict rest on the vendor pages; the identity kind, the encryption add-on and the seller history are not stated on them.
